stories.title: Pokimane and Atrioc's old deepfake scandal returns to the creator conversation
paragraphs: Pokimane revisited the 2023 nonconsensual deepfake episode after seeing Atrioc at the wedding of mutual friends Ludwig Ahgren and QTCinderella. Coverage says she described feeling uncomfortable and publicly humiliated; she also said she was not trying to cancel him.

Atrioc responded on stream, and reports say he withdrew from a TwitchCon 2026 panel. The episode has reopened debate over the effects of the original misconduct and how the creator community handles a person's return.

Other streamers commented, and sampled Reddit threads drew hundreds to thousands of votes. Those are visible discussion points, not a measure of overall sentiment; some reactions attacked Pokimane personally.

scoreNotes.general: A high-profile creator dispute drew multiple responses and visible discussion, though the saved coverage is mostly entertainment reporting and sampled posts.
scoreNotes.heat: Several creators weighed in and Reddit threads showed substantial attention; those samples do not represent the whole streaming audience.
scoreNotes.time: Pokimane's posts and Atrioc's response were reported October 26–27, within the current collection window.
scoreNotes.ethos: Dexerto and Spilled summarize the exchange, while the saved results do not include direct posts or a full transcript of Atrioc's stream.

stories.title: Meta delays creator-facing terms change after backlash over AI training
paragraphs: Meta has delayed a planned update to its commercial terms after creators and publishers objected to language they feared could permit their work to be used for AI training. Reports say the rollout moved from October 30 to November 20.
The dispute has expanded beyond individual photographers: Digiday describes publishers coordinating their response and says Meta wants more time to explain the changes to partners and stakeholders.

The delay gives affected businesses more time to assess the proposal, but it does not resolve how Meta will use covered material. The saved evidence does not establish the final terms or whether the change will be altered again.

scoreNotes.general: The proposed terms affect publishers and creators whose material may be used by Meta, and the delay followed coordinated pushback.
scoreNotes.heat: Reports describe escalating objections from creators and publishers, but the saved results provide no reliable audience measure.
scoreNotes.time: The delay was reported in the October 26–28 research window.
scoreNotes.ethos: Digital Camera World and Digiday report a delay and stakeholder concerns; the full final terms and scope remain unsettled.

stories.title: Auroch Digital says layoffs will affect about a quarter of its staff
paragraphs: Auroch Digital, the studio behind Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun, began a redundancy consultation affecting around a quarter of its employees, according to PC Gamer and PocketGamer.biz.
The announcement appeared in posts that were later deleted, then was reposted on October 28. The saved coverage does not establish why the posts were removed or identify the affected roles.
The scale points to a major change for the studio, but the available evidence does not connect the cuts to a specific game cancellation or establish a broader publisher-wide restructuring.

scoreNotes.general: The cuts are a significant studio-level consequence for a known independent developer, though the saved evidence does not show wider restructuring.
scoreNotes.heat: Around a quarter of the studio's staff are affected, a substantial share, but broad audience reaction is not documented.
scoreNotes.time: The layoff announcement and its reappearance in coverage were dated October 27–28.
scoreNotes.ethos: PC Gamer and PocketGamer.biz report the same approximate scale; the studio's original posts were deleted and the saved results do not explain why.
